## Sales grew 15% to $479k
layout: section
kicker: Part 1 | Sales

## We beat last year in 11 of 12 months
layout: chart
kicker: Sales
subtitle: Monthly revenue, $k
takeaway: December still makes the year, but spring grew too

```chart
type: line
number_format: '#,##0'
labels: false
legend: true
colors: [muted, accent]
categories: [Oct, Nov, Dec, Jan, Feb, Mar, Apr, May, Jun, Jul, Aug, Sep]
series:
  - name: FY2025
    values: [31, 44, 62, 24, 26, 29, 30, 33, 35, 32, 34, 37]
  - name: FY2026

```

Notes:
June was the one month down, when two weeks of web orders shipped late after the cure room overheated.
Source: Soap Club sales ledger, FY2025 and FY2026, revenue net of discounts.

## Fig & Black Pepper grew fastest
layout: table
kicker: Sales
subtitle: Units sold by scent, FY2026
takeaway: Rose Clay and Charcoal & Mint lost ground; one of them goes

| Scent | Units | vs FY2025 | Share |
|---|---|---|---|
| Oat & Lavender | 18,200 | +16% | 36% |
| Cedar Smoke | 10,900 | +22% | 21% |
| Salt Scrub | 8,600 | +9% | 17% |
| Fig & Black Pepper | 6,100 | +41% | 12% |
| Rose Clay | 4,300 | -6% | 8% |
| Charcoal & Mint | 2,900 | -18% | 6% |

Notes:
51,000 bars in total. Fig & Black Pepper launched in FY2025 and found its buyers this year.
Source: Soap Club production log, FY2026, bars wrapped and sold.

## Costs rose faster than prices
layout: section
kicker: Part 2 | Operations

## Labor is the biggest cost in a bar
layout: chart
kicker: Operations
subtitle: Where the $9 price of a web bar goes
takeaway: A second soap maker costs less than the overtime we paid

```chart
type: doughnut
number_format: '0"%"'
labels: true
legend: true
colors: [primary, accent, muted, "B9A9A4", "5E5B66"]
categories: [Labor, Margin, Oils and butters, Shipping, Wrapping]
series:
  - name: Share of price
    values: [31, 26, 22, 12, 9]
```

Notes:
Overtime in November and December came to $14k, about two thirds of a part-time maker's annual pay.
Source: Soap Club cost model, FY2026 averages for a bar sold on the web.

## Cheaper shipping offset dearer oil
layout: chart
kicker: Operations
subtitle: Change in cost per bar against FY2025, cents
takeaway: Cost per bar rose 4 cents in all; olive oil did most of it

```chart
type: bar
number_format: '+0;-0;0'
labels: true
legend: false
categories: [Olive oil, Fragrance, Shea butter, Wrapping paper, Shipping]
series:
  - name: Change in cents
    values: [6, 3, 1, -2, -4]
```

Notes:
The shipping saving came from moving web orders to a flat-rate carrier in February. The paper saving is the new Dumbder Nifftlin wrap.
Source: supplier invoices and the carrier statement, FY2025 and FY2026.

## Two corporate accounts, two asks
layout: comparison
kicker: Operations
left-heading: Dumbder Nifftlin Paper Co.
right-heading: Cubicle 9 Enterprises

### left
- 400 gift boxes each December
- Wants its logo on the wrap
- Pays in 60 days
- Renews in January

### right
- Bars for 12 office washrooms
- A monthly order in plain wrap
- Asked for a refill pump
- Renews in March

### left-logo
![Dumbder Nifftlin Paper Co. logo](assets/dumbder-nifftlin-logo.png)

### right-logo
![Cubicle 9 Enterprises logo](assets/cubicle-nine-logo.png)

Notes:
Corporate was 7% of revenue, $36k across the two accounts.
Source: Soap Club sales ledger, FY2026, corporate channel.

## What worked and what did not
layout: two-col
kicker: Operations

### left
- **Worked:** the gift box sold out
- Stockists reordered by email
- Market days paid off by noon

### right
- **Did not:** the refill pouch
- Rose Clay cracked in the heat
- Web orders shipped late in June

Notes:
The gift box sold out by December 10. Stockists reordered with no sales calls. The refill pouch sold 40 units all year.

label2: Range
label3: Costs

### text1
- Grow from **4 to 10** stockists, starting with Larkspur Market

### text2
- Retire one weak scent and launch one **winter** scent

### text3
- Fix olive oil prices for **12 months** with one supplier

### text4
- Hire a second soap maker by **March**
